general.title: General information to asynchronous Service execution and OPC UA

runs.text: A Server cannot always answer a request in the time its Client is willing to wait. A gateway asked to distribute a TrustList to the devices behind it, an aggregating Server asked to write a value that lives elsewhere, a Server asked to run a Method that turns a machine: the work outlasts the request, and OPC UA has no way to say so.

What the Client gets today is a timeout, which does not distinguish a Server that failed from a Server that is still working. It therefore cannot safely retry: repeating a certificate update or a Method that moves an axis is not the same as repeating a read.

This document defines asynchronous Service execution, which is the missing answer. A Server that cannot respond in time parks the request and says so with a StatusCode that already exists for the purpose, together with a hint about when to ask again. A new Service, Continue, collects the response when it is ready, keyed on the request handle the Client already assigned and the Cancel Service already uses. It is a proposed addition to the base OPC UA namespace, not a new companion namespace.
Deferral is for a Service call whose answer may legitimately outlast the call. Three families of use case motivate it.

Gateways and aggregating Servers. A Server that fronts other devices or other Servers cannot answer faster than the slowest thing it has to reach. The certificate push Methods of OPC 10000-12 are the sharpest example — one call on the gateway becomes one exchange per device behind it — and Annex B works such a deployment through in full. The same shape appears whenever an aggregating Server forwards a Write or a Method call to an underlying Server.

Operations that change the physical world. A Method that moves an axis, runs a recipe or commissions a device takes as long as the equipment takes. Today a Client either holds a request open for the duration or loses track of the outcome; with a deferral it collects the result when the work is done, and the audit trail records the outcome whether or not it does.

Clients that cannot stay connected. A commissioning tool, a scheduled job or a cloud-hosted Client may not survive an hour-long operation. Durable deferral lets a later Session of the same user identity collect a response the Session that asked for it never saw.

Deferral is not a replacement for a Subscription, which reports what a Client did not ask for, nor for the ticket Methods that individual specifications already define, which continue to work unchanged. Annex C sets out which mechanism suits which shape of problem.

A Server that is the front of something else cannot answer within the time its Client will wait. A gateway asked to distribute a TrustList to the devices behind it, an aggregating Server asked to write a value that lives in an underlying Server, a Server asked to run a Method that turns a machine: the work outlasts
, and OPC UA has nothing to say about it. The Client gets

A long poll, solving a different problem — a stream of unsolicited notifications — by keeping requests in flight, which is exactly what a Client cannot afford for an operation that takes an hour.

A Client that waits an hour holds a socket, a thread and a Session for an hour, learns nothing while it waits, and loses everything if the connection blinks. The point of a deferral is that the Client can go away.

runs.text: This is deliberate, and it is the difference between a mechanism that solves the problem and one that moves it. A Server cannot know whether a response it transmitted arrived: if the connection fails between transmission and receipt — which is precisely the condition that makes long operations hard — a delete-on-delivery rule leaves the Client with an effect it caused and an outcome it can never learn. That is the failure this specification exists to remove, and reintroducing it at the last step would defeat the whole mechanism.

The namespace metadata provide standardized information about the elements of this namespace, which an aggregating Server relies on. All Nodes defined by this document are static: they are identical in every Server, including the Value Attribute.

The information is provided as an Object of type NamespaceMetadataType, a component of the Namespaces Object of the Server Object. The NamespaceMetadataType ObjectType and its Properties are defined in OPC 10000-5. The same version information is carried by the ModelTableEntry of the UANodeSet XML file.

The IsNamespaceSubset Property is True because the UANodeSet XML file contains only the Nodes this document adds, not the complete namespace. A Server that exposes the whole namespace sets it to False.

Namespaces are used by OPC UA to create unique identifiers across different naming authorities. The NodeId and BrowseName Attributes are identifiers. A Node in the AddressSpace is unambiguously identified by its NodeId; a BrowseName is not unique and is used to build a browse path or to name a standard Property.
